Algebraic Riccati equations

Source: R/riccati.R
ctrl_care.Rd

ctrl_care() computes the stabilizing solution of the continuous time algebraic Riccati equation $$A^\top P + P A - (P B + S) R^{-1} (B^\top P + S^\top) + Q = 0,$$ and ctrl_dare() the stabilizing solution of the discrete time equation $$A^\top P A - P - (A^\top P B + S)(R + B^\top P B)^{-1} (B^\top P A + S^\top) + Q = 0.$$

Usage

ctrl_care(A, B, Q, R, S = NULL, check_weights = TRUE)

ctrl_dare(A, B, Q, R, S = NULL, check_weights = TRUE)

Arguments

A

State matrix (n x n).

B

Input matrix (n x m).

Q

State weight (n x n, symmetric).

R

Input weight (m x m, symmetric positive definite).

S

Optional cross weight (n x m); defaults to zero.

check_weights

If TRUE (default), require \(\begin{pmatrix} Q & S \\ S^\top & R\end{pmatrix} \succeq 0\), the condition under which the equation describes a well-posed LQ problem. Set to FALSE to solve indefinite equations (for example in H-infinity synthesis).

Value

A list of class ctrl_riccati with P (stabilizing solution), K (the associated gain \(R^{-1}(B^\top P + S^\top)\) or \((R + B^\top P B)^{-1}(B^\top P A + S^\top)\)), poles (eigenvalues of \(A - B K\)), residual (relative Frobenius residual of the equilibrated equation), symmetry_error, rcond_u11 and discrete.

Details

Both solvers use the extended (Arnold and Laub) matrix pencil of dimension \(2n + m\), compress away the input block with an orthogonal QR factorization (so R is never inverted explicitly), and compute an ordered generalized real Schur decomposition with LAPACK dgges that places the n stable eigenvalues first. The solution is \(P = U_{21} U_{11}^{-1}\), obtained with a linear solve. The discrete pencil formulation does not require A to be invertible.

The stabilizing solution exists and is unique when R is positive definite, \((A, B)\) is stabilizable and the pencil has no eigenvalues on the stability boundary (guaranteed, for example, when \(Q - S R^{-1} S^\top \succeq 0\) and the corresponding pair is detectable). When the boundary condition fails, or when \(U_{11}\) is singular, an error is raised rather than an invalid solution returned. A solution whose relative residual exceeds 1e-6, or whose closed loop is not stable, raises an error. The returned object reports the relative residual, the symmetry error and the closed-loop eigenvalues so that the result can be verified. Before solving, the equation is equilibrated: a symplectic diagonal state scaling from balancing the Hamiltonian matrix (so states in very different units carry comparable weight), a common time scale (continuous time) and a common weight factor, all by powers of two. The residual is reported for the equilibrated equation. The Schur method is backward stable in the normwise sense, so weights that differ by many orders of magnitude within one state or input direction can still lose relative accuracy.

References

Arnold, W. F. and Laub, A. J. (1984). Generalized eigenproblem algorithms and software for algebraic Riccati equations. Proceedings of the IEEE, 72(12), 1746-1754.

Examples

# Scalar CARE with known solution sqrt(2) - 1
ctrl_care(-1, 1, 1, 1)$P
#>           [,1]
#> [1,] 0.4142136
# Scalar DARE with known solution (1 + sqrt(5)) / 2
ctrl_dare(1, 1, 1, 1)$P
#>          [,1]
#> [1,] 1.618034
